item.title: Canceled Hideo Kojima Game P.T. Is Making a Comeback
item.description:
P.T. is making an unexpected comeback more than a decade after Hideo Kojima's infamous horror teaser disappeared from the PlayStation Store, as a fan developer rebuilds it as a native PC port. The project could give P.T. a new lease on life while staying much closer to the original PS4 release than the many fan remakes that followed.

Released unexpectedly on PS4 in August 2014, P.T. initially hid its true identity behind the fictional 7780s Studio name but quickly became a sensation in the horror gaming world. Famously, players who finally solved its notoriously obscure puzzles were treated to a final sequence revealing that the short horror game was actually a playable teaser for Silent Hills , a new entry involving Metal Gear Solid 's Hideo Kojima, filmmaker Guillermo del Toro, and Norman Reedus. Unfortunately, Konami canceled Silent Hills in 2015 as Kojima's relationship with the publisher fell apart, subsequently removing P.T. from the PlayStation Store and eventually making it impossible to redownload, even for players who had previously claimed it.

Kojima's Next Game 'OD' Gets Positive Update

Three years since its announcement, Hideo Kojima and Jordan Peele's horror game OD is still nowhere to be seen, but there is some good news at least.

By Dominik Bošnjak

P.T. Is Being Rebuilt as a Native PC Game

Kojima's lost horror demo might be getting a second life thanks to a native PC port being created by LoreanXavier. The developer says the project "isn't an emulator, a wrapper, or a remake" in another engine. Instead, the developer is reverse-engineering the PS4 executable and rebuilding P.T. 's logic and rendering in C++ and Vulkan, with the port running on data files from an original copy of the game. Most of the experience is already functional, including its Lua scripts, cutscenes, Lisa's animations, sound behavior, controller vibration, and infamous voice-recognition sequence, with 30 minutes of gameplay available on YouTube. The build also supports 60-plus FPS, higher resolutions, mouse and keyboard input, modern controllers, and optional AMD FSR 3.1, although there is no release date yet.

The way that P.T. accomplished so much with so little might be one of the game's most enduring elements, influencing much of the horror genre to come. Most of the experience traps the player inside the same L-shaped hallway, but each loop changes small details until the space becomes impossible to trust. Doors shift, objects appear, the radio speaks directly to the player, while P.T. 's main antagonist, Lisa, can suddenly stand somewhere she wasn't moments earlier. Conventional combat and UI are also barely present, leaving players to study the environment and wonder whether they missed something or are just getting in their own heads. P.T. proved that repetition and uncertainty could be just as frightening as a room full of monsters.

That formula spread quickly once P.T. disappeared. Allison Road was one of the earliest projects to chase a similar mood, while games like Visage and Layers of Fear leaned into first-person exploration, ordinary domestic spaces as horror settings, shifting environments, and psychological scares. Direct fan recreations followed too, but those rebuilt the teaser in other engines. LoreanXavier's project marks the first effort to preserve and translate the game's code and gameplay behavior rather than approximating it.

Canceled Hideo Kojima Game P.T. Is Making a Comeback

Pokemon TCG Fans Can Get Free Cards, But There's a Catch

While the world around P.T. has changed and moved on, that PS4 demo still remains stuck in 2014, and that may be why it remains so fascinating. Following a long hiatus, Konami has finally revived Silent Hill and just released Silent Hill: Townfall , its first full-length first-person entry, while Kojima has built Death Stranding and is now developing the horror project OD and the action-espionage game Physint . Meanwhile, P.T. never got a future of its own, yet its influence never really faded and is felt today. The fact that someone is still trying to bring the original experience back 12 years later says plenty about how much that single hallway changed horror games and the industry at large.

P.T.

item.title: 6 January 2027 LEGO Sets Quietly Detailed in New Leak
item.description:
A new leak has revealed fresh details about six LEGO sets reportedly planned for January 2027. The upcoming lineup, which was already mentioned in a prior insider report, is expected to expand LEGO's long-running City theme.

The six products are part of a significantly larger rumored wave. A July leak listing 19 purported LEGO City sets planned for early 2027 already disclosed their product numbers, possible names, and approximate prices, but offered comparatively little information about what they would actually include.

Iconic LEGO Vehicle Finally Getting UCS Treatment in August 2027

A recurring LEGO vehicle is finally said to be getting an Ultimate Collector Series (UCS) treatment more than 22 years since its original debut.

By Dominik Bošnjak

LEGO City's 2027 Lineup Is Starting to Take Shape

An October 4 report from longtime LEGO leaker carter_bricks04 expanded on the Danish toymaker's rumored January 2027 lineup with descriptions for half a dozen sets, citing premature listings from an unnamed online retailer. The new information covers sets 60521, 60527, 60530, 60532, 60534, and 60541, listing some of their alleged vehicle and minifigure counts, plus details on several accessories and features.

Set

Price

Leaked Description

60521

$34.99

Ages 6+; two vehicles; two drivers

60527

$59.99

Williams and Aston Martin F1 cars; four minifigures; pit wall; screens; launcher

60530

$12.99

Mercedes-AMG race car; F1 driver minifigure in team colors

60532

$9.99

Police vehicle with a cell; police officer; thief; handcuffs

60534

$59.99

Three vehicles; three minifigures; multiple accessories

60541

$29.99

Three vehicles; three minifigures; fire, police, and construction theme

F1 LEGO Sets Stand Out in the Leaked Descriptions

Set 60527 stands out as the subject of perhaps the most substantial information update. An earlier rumor had already linked it to Williams and Aston Martin, while the purported retailer description now points to two cars, four minifigures, a pit wall, some form of screen-equipped accessory, and a launcher. Set 60530 appears considerably smaller, consisting of a Mercedes-AMG racing car and an F1 driver dressed in the team's colors. If accurate, both would extend Formula 1's presence within LEGO City as part of LEGO and F1's broader partnership.

Recommended for You
Hand-picked by GameRant editors
GameRant may earn an affiliate commission from links on this page.

The rest of the leak provides additional details on several more traditional concepts from the LEGO City theme. Set 60534 reportedly includes three vehicles and three minifigures, while 60541 lists the same totals for a product involving firefighters, police, and construction. The smaller 60532 product appears to center on a police chase, complete with an officer, thief, handcuffs, and a vehicle with a holding cell. Meanwhile, 60521 is described as a 6+ set containing two vehicles and two drivers, consistent with the vehicle-heavy approach seen across recent LEGO City lineups.

6 January 2027 LEGO Sets Quietly Detailed in New Leak
Iconic LEGO Vehicle Finally Getting UCS Treatment in August 2027
Massive LEGO Dragon Ball Set Officially Announced for November 2026
LEGO Is Saying Goodbye To 34 Sets At the End of 2026

Some of the leaked retailer wording is noticeably awkward. Phrases such as "Boat Racing Car," "box with screens," and the description of 60534 as involving "the police truck and its LEGO City car" suggest that the text may have been translated or otherwise adapted from material that was not intended as finalized English marketing copy. As a result, the leak should not necessarily be taken as evidence of the official names for LEGO's rumored January 2027 sets.

item.title: 5 Open-World Games Where Exploring Too Early Is A Huge Mistake
item.description:
Open-world games are all about exploration, or at least that's one of their biggest appeals. Every fan of the genre knows the feeling of being unable to sit still, especially during those first few hours when the entire map is unfamiliar and every road seems exciting. However, even the most experienced adventurers often overestimate themselves, especially early in a game.

Most times, this doesn't lead to anything worse than an embarrassingly quick U-turn. However, there are some games that punish early exploration faster than you can say "skill issue." Of course, you shouldn't be discouraged from wandering off the main path altogether. Sometimes, coming back and conquering an area you failed as a newbie makes the experience more rewarding. Here are some open-world games that make you think twice before wandering too far too soon.

Final Fantasy 2

One Wrong Turn Is All It Takes

As with any game, looking hard enough for flaws in Final Fantasy 2 will probably uncover as many as your heart desires. Its dungeon design, activity-based progression, and counterintuitive leveling system are only the beginning; the cherry on top is the way the game handles early exploration, and frankly, exploration in general. Much of the overworld is accessible surprisingly early, and even the paths are designed in such a way that they seem like they're inviting players to wander wherever they please.

11 Open-World Games Worth Playing Just For Their Exploration

Most open-world games feature exploration, but these titles absolutely nail this part of the gameplay loop. Travel, explore, and discover.

6
By Mac Wheeler

The problem is that enemy difficulty can change very quickly and unexpectedly. One wrong turn can suddenly put an inexperienced party up against monsters that are way stronger than expected. Moreover, if you don't run into enemies, you're most probably going to find yourself at a dead end. Few players expect every single path and dungeon to be meaningful, but Final Fantasy 2 is so hostile to curiosity that it almost becomes a parody. If you have played games like Dark Souls and thought they were punishing, just wait until you give Final Fantasy 2 a shot.

Fallout: New Vegas

Some Paths Are Better Left Alone

Technically, Fallout: New Vegas gives the Courier a lot of freedom almost immediately after handing over control to the player, but that doesn't mean you can just safely take any path you want. Generally, when you start the game at Goodsprings, the lights of New Vegas are visible, and you'll be tempted to take the northern route because it looks like such a convenient shortcut.

6 Best Open World Games That Don't Hold Your Hand, Ranked

These open-world games refuse to guide you, as getting lost is the point. From STALKER to Morrowind, they reward the bold and punish the careless.

5
By Mark Smith

This alone should make the alarms in your head ring, but for those who have the survival instinct of a houseplant, I'll help out: if you do that, you'll find yourself in the Sloan and Quarry Junction, where even the locals warn travelers about raging Deathclaws. Moreover, the further you go, the higher your chances of meeting Cazadore, so if you're a lower level, this trip will end extremely quickly. Keep in mind that even the official game guide describes the Quarry as one of the most dangerous locations on the map, especially for those who are below Level 15.

Subnautica

Curiosity Killed The Cat

When I hear the name Subnautica , the first word that comes to my mind is "beautiful." A colorful world full of fascinating creatures, locations packed with resources, and lots and lots of exploration opportunities. Well, at least for those who are not just starting out. Early on, your oxygen is limited, so long expeditions are definitely out of the question.

10 Best Open-World Games If You Want An Escape From Reality, Ranked

Struggling to deal with the real world? These open-world games have you covered, offering expansive worlds and lengthy play times as a distraction.

5
By Peter Morics

Moreover, venturing into the wrong areas too early will often lead to unfortunate events, increasing your chances of encountering some not-so-friendly Reaper Leviathans. Don't even think about wandering off further before you are ready. For example, the closer you get to the Lost River, the more hostile the fauna becomes.

Generally, Subnautica encourages exploration, but there is a reason why it's better to leave some areas for later. The more you play, the bigger the oxygen tanks you'll acquire. Your vehicles will get better, and depth upgrades will help you reach more dangerous areas. In other words, make sure you have progressed enough to be properly equipped before swimming deeper.

The Long Dark

Going Too Far Can Cost You Everything

If you're up for a real survival challenge, The Long Dark will not disappoint. The game is set in a post-apocalyptic Canadian wilderness, and even though it looks like a prehistoric monster will attack you at any second, no such encounter will happen. Instead, you'll be faced with starvation, freezing cold, blizzards, and darkness.

Just like in real nature, every decision you make has to be based on how much stamina you have left, how much daylight remains, and whether your supplies will be enough to keep you warm and fed. This means that exploring is never safe, let alone for inexperienced players who are still learning the ropes.

8 Open‑World Games That Reward Solo Survival, Ranked

Teaming up might make these open-world games easier, but playing alone can be even more satisfying.

By Ollie Tuscarny

This is especially true because the game does not allow manual saves in its survival mode; once you die, your death is permanent. Overall, wandering around is almost never safe, but not knowing the map, combined with not knowing your character's limits, is a recipe for a slow and painful death. If all of that is not enough of a warning to be careful at the beginning, keep in mind that The Long Dark is one of the hardest open-world survival games out there.

Kenshi

Bravery Won't Keep You Alive

Kenshi is an open-world survival game that never goes easy on you just because you're a newbie. There is no special treatment for anyone, and enemy strength does not magically shift to match your experience level. If you wander into somewhere dangerous, you'll have to bear the consequences. Keep in mind that you can get robbed, enslaved, or badly wounded by your enemies, which is especially bad during the beginning stages of the game.

That's why it's not surprising that the first skill you have to develop in Kenshi is running. This is a useful skill in the game in general, as it will help you later on as well, but as a beginner, you absolutely need to move a lot to improve your athletics before even thinking about walking off the main path.

item.title: How to Increase Flight Power in Aion 2
item.description:
In Aion 2 , characters unlock the ability to fly early in the tutorial. Short of teleportation, it is the fastest way to get around the map in this game, but unfortunately, how long you can fly without running out of steam is limited by a stamina resource called Flight Power, which recovers slowly over time.

This guide covers how you can increase your Flight Power as well as how you can use flight movement techs to use your current Flight Power more efficiently, flying for longer distances while consuming less stamina.

All Aion 2 Redeem Codes (October 2026)

Here are all active redeem codes and coupons for Aion 2 added by NCSoft and how to claim them in-game.

By Hamza Haq

How to Increase Flight Power in Aion 2

Flight Power is a mechanic in Aion 2 that dictates how long you can use your Wings in order to fly. The only way to increase Flight Power is by collecting new Wings . Every Wing comes with two stats: Owned Effect and Equipped Effect.

Owned Effects are effects that apply regardless of whether an item is equipped or merely sitting in your inventory. Equipped Effects, on the other hand, only apply when the item is equipped and are removed when you take it off.

Flight Power is exclusively an Owned Effect on Wings , meaning the more Wings you collect on a character, the higher their Flight Power will become.

You’ll unlock Intermediate, Superior, and Ultimate Daeva Wings by completing Ascension main story quests while leveling. Prioritize them whenever available to increase your Flight Power quickly.

There are 28 obtainable Wings in Aion 2 , and you can check appearances, sources, and applied effects (including Flight Power) for each and every one in the Wings tab after you unlock the ability to fly during the tutorial.

The Wings from Aion 2 ’s Founder’s Packs do not give Flight Power.

In fact, if you open the Wings tab (Alt + C) , you can see your current Flight Power under the “All Applied Effects” tab in the “All Owned Effects” section. The higher this number is, the longer you can fly, and the only way to increase it is to get more Wings.

Some titles, like Professional Extractor and Cogni Executioner, grant you a stat called Flight Speed. This is not the same as Flight Power. As the name suggests, instead of increasing your total flight stamina, this increases the speed at which you fly.

How to Do the “Fly Tech” in Aion 2

There is a flying movement tech in Aion 2 that lets you use the same amount of Flight Power to travel a greater distance. Here’s how it works:

  1. Press V to start flying.
  2. Hold W to move forward, and press Shift to give yourself a boost.
  3. Immediately after pressing Shift, press V to disable flight. Your character will come out of flight, still carrying the momentum from the previous boost.
  4. Tap V again to resume flight mid-air.
  5. Repeat from Step 1.

item.title: Control Resonant: All Artifacts, Locations & Effects
item.description:
In Control Resonant , Artifacts are among the most powerful pieces of equipment Dylan can wield. While some of these elusive items grant flat-out passive benefits, others act as a double-edged sword, offering massive power spikes at the cost of noticeable debuffs. Since players can equip only a limited number of Artifacts at once, finding the right synergy is crucial for surviving the game's toughest encounters. To help you perfect Dylan's build, here are all the Artifacts in Control Resonant , alongside what effects they offer and their locations.

Updated October 4, 2026, by Ayyoun Ali : All missing artifacts have been added, and the list is now complete.

Control Resonant: The Last Taxi Quest Walkthrough (All Locations & Solutions)

Track down all seven anomalous taxis hidden throughout the map to complete 'The Last Taxi' quest in Control Resonant.

By Ayyoun Ali

List of All Artifacts, Their Effects, and Locations in Control Resonant

There are a total of 43 artifacts in Control Resonant that are divided into different categories based on the effect they provide. Here's a quick explainer on different types of artifacts to help you grasp the gist of what they do.

Some Artifacts belonging to the same family/type cannot be equipped together.

  • Survival : The effects are mainly focused on Dylan's health and HP recovery.
  • Combat : Focuses on Dylan's combat abilities, like damage and Falter output.
  • Exploration : Helps Dylan with exploration, like helping him detect crates from afar.
  • Special : Wildcard Artifacts that come with special conditions that provide massive buffs at the cost of massive debuffs.

Players will most likely receive Untapped Artifacts , which are basically a recipe to craft that artifact in the Gap. Here are the sources that give players Artifacts in Control Resonant .

  • Pre-order & Deluxe Edition bonuses
  • Main & Side Missions
  • Purchasing from Vendors
  • Leveling up Zones
  • Defeating Resonant (main bosses)

With that out of the way, let's get to the list of Artifacts.

Recycling artifacts will refund resources, but remove them completely from your inventory. You'll need to craft them again before use.

Image

Artifact

Effects

Location

Lockpick's Tool

Next combat ability after a perfect dodge does not consume Power.

Preorder Bonus.

Wallet

Combat abilities consume Health when out of Power. Deactivates when Health falls below 5%.

Deluxe Edition.

Stellar Bracelet

When Shield is destroyed/broken, Dylan restores a small amount of Health.

Vendor in Central Zone.

Bug Spray

Adds +30% Damage and Falter against mold, but Dylan receives twice as much Infected buildup.

Badge 11-60

Dylan takes significantly less damage from environmental hazards.

Defeat Downtown Resonant "The Artist" during the Prologue.

World Tour Tickets

Combat abilities deal +100 damage, but Power is capped at 50%.

Vendor on the 15th floor of the Evac Building in the Evacuation Zone.

(Unlocked after Evacuation Procedures Main Story Mission)

Molding Bar

Grants immunity to Infected status and buffs Dylan's Damage and Falter against Mold enemies. However, health is capped at 50%.

Vendor in The Park Zone.

Medical Alert Bands

Adds +25% Falter to all attacks if Dylan's health is below 25%.

Reward for Carbon Copy Part 3 side story.

Brass Dusters

Combat abilities deal +50% damage but no Falter.

Complete the New Growth side story.

Lighter

Increases Dylan's Burn resistance.

Defeat the Central Resonant Boss.

Ornate Buckle

Executing enemies recovers a large amount of Power, but damage taken by Dylan is increased by +30%.

Vendor in the Evacuation Zone.

Shiny Pebbles

Slowly restores health up to 50% when using the Gravity Anomaly (Shift).

Complete the Freeze Frame side story.

Unfinished Lollipop

Increases Damage done by secondary melee form by +10%.

Complete all 11 Dylan Sketchbook drawings.

Trusted Spanner

Increases Dylan's Raw damage output by +15%.

Complete Every Dog Has Her Day side story.

Whetstone

Adds +20% Damage but reduces Falter by -20%.

Complete A New Directive side story.

Golden Earrings

Increases Falter by +20%, but reduces Damage by -30%.

Defeat the Underpass Resonant boss.

Scrunchie

Increases Damage from Primary Aberrant forms by +10%.

Find all FBC Testing Facilities and complete the Unsupervised Science side story.

1996 Commemorative Coin

Health elements become more effective and restore a larger amount of HP.

Defeat the Unknown Resonant boss.

Compact

Critical Hits deal +50% more damage, but deal -30% less Falter.

Defeat the Unknown Resonant boss in New Game Plus mode.

Worn Eraser

Increases Dylan's resistance to all negative effects.

Defeat the Final Story Boss of Control Resonant .

Bout Guard

Increases Dylan's Power recovery by +50%, but he takes +20% more damage.

Complete "The Complete Set" side story.

Lost Prescription

Adds a +30% chance to restore a small amount of health on every Perfect Dodge.

Vendor in the Downtown Zone.

Coffee Cup

Health regenerates slowly outside combat.

Complete the "Last Taxi" side story.

Wad of Cash

Makes the Command ability cost 1 fewer Command charge.

Vendor in the Unknown Zone.

(Available during Epilogue in Dylan's Apartment)

Fork

Increases Dylan's Sharp damage output by +15%.

Complete Mapping the New York side story. (Activating Map Kits in 7 zones)

Catnip Toy

Significantly reduces damage received by falling into the void.

Complete Into the Valley of Death side story.

Framing Hammer

Combat abilities deal +30% Falter but no damage at all.

Vendor in the Underpass Zone.

Bar Blade

Health regenerates slowly when a summoned ally is nearby.

Complete The Party Won't Stop side story.

Spray Paint

Increases Dylan's Blunt damage output by +15%.

Vendor in the West Incursion Zone.

Amulet

Increases Critical Chance for all melee attacks by +5%.

Defeat the West Incursion Zone Resonant boss.

Face Mask

Gives Dylan resistance to Infected status by increasing the time it takes to build up.

Defeat The Park Resonant boss.

Mother's Locket

Adds +25% Damage when Health falls below 25%.

Complete Carbon Copy Part 1 side story.

Heart Monitor

Prevents death and revives Dylan once with 20% HP, but breaks upon activation.

Complete Urban Survival side story.

Practice Knot

Adds +15% Falter to all attacks on Heavy enemies.

Complete Crossing the Threshold side story.

Feeding Bottle

Adds +30% Power recovery when Dylan is affected by Infected or Burn statuses.

Complete the Panopticon Service Request side story.

Novelty Magnet

Nearby small resource crates are marked on the radar (mini-map).

Get a high score at the Shum III arcade cabinet in Dylan's Apartment.

Paper Plane

Increases Power for every attack Dylan does while airborne.

Vendor in Unknown Zone.

Fingerboard

Adds +25% Damage and Falter while using a Gravity Anomaly (Shift).

Vendor in Downtown Zone.

Old Subway Card

Significantly increases the Rush ability's duration.

Defeat Hedron Axiom - Apex post-game boss located in the Underpass north of Tubes Island.

Lit Sparkler

A Perfect Dodge makes Dylan's next dodge create an explosive charge that deals Fire Damage to nearby enemies.

Reward for reaching zone level 14 in Downtown.

Energy Drink

Adds +30% Critical Chance to all melee attacks when Dylan is at full health. However, he'll take +20% more damage.

Reward for reaching zone level 12 in Unknown.

The Weekend Crossword

Increases damage done by Combo Finishers by +15%.

Reward for reaching zone level 13 in Central.

(Currently bugged as of update 1.4)

Water Pistol

Critical Hits deal +50% damage to Hiss Shields.

TBA.

You'll need to craft only 30 of the artifacts above to unlock the Paranatural Artisan trophy in Control Resonant .
